@frenck Sorry to disturb you, but I keep having issues with pylint. I don't see what I'm doing wrong and on my dev environment my tests pass and I don't have any issue in pylint. 

I tried to do the same as in e.g. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/ea9d312b455fabc76e4dfb73dcbfde79c08ed752/homeassistant/components/brother/const.py, defining tuple with SensorEntityDescription, but pylint keeps complaining about the tuple being unsubscriptable. Hope you can help me out.

@frenck I fixed the requested changes. The only thing I notice is that the `state_class` and `device_class` are only visible as sensor attribute after a clean new installation of the integration, existing installations seem to stick without these attributes and hence also not show up in the energy view. I checked the entity registry, and they don't seem to be updated on an system with existing solarlog integration. Is there a way to force an update of the entity registry? 

HA system with existing solarlog integration

```
            {
                "entity_id": "sensor.solarlog_yield_total",
                "config_entry_id": "55ccbd7e703a84d36672efdf211bf61c",
                "device_id": "3f493e769d220d97f089187a93f13255",
                "area_id": null,
                "unique_id": "55ccbd7e703a84d36672efdf211bf61c_yield_total",
                "platform": "solarlog",
                "name": null,

                "capabilities": {},
                "supported_features": 0,
                "device_class": null,
                "unit_of_measurement": "kWh",
                "original_name": "solarlog yield total",
                "original_icon": "mdi:solar-power"
            },
```

HA system with fresh new solarlog integration

```
            {
                "entity_id": "sensor.solarlog_yield_total",
                "config_entry_id": "b22363a7e563e9ab9627c0c91a9d2bd3",

                "capabilities": {
                    "state_class": "measurement"
                },
                "supported_features": 0,
                "device_class": "energy",
                "unit_of_measurement": "kWh",
                "original_name": "solarlog yield total",
                "original_icon": "mdi:solar-power"
            },
```

Edit: nevermind, turned out that I was not using the modified version, but still the built in version.
@ludeeus @frenck All requested changes have been made.
Please make sure the build passes.
Sorry @frenck The build passes now correctly
@frenck I've also updated the docs with the above changed units in a separate PR.

review_comments: Doesn't this have a unit? What type of information is this?

According to the sunwatcher pypi and package and solarlog docs it is defined as current total AC Power of all consumption meters (in W) divided by Total output AC power of all the inverters (in W). So, this will be a percentage, I think. (Can’t check it, as I don’t have a consumption meter onnette. Will fix the unit tomorrow as well.
Fixed it. I changed the unit of measurement to PERCENTAGE and and the device class is set to "power_factor"

I don't think this is the correct unit of measurement. I'm assuming this means Watt-peak, but that's not a scientific unit of measurement but what kind of power measurement this is. The unit should just be Watt (POWER_WATT) and we should specify that it's peak power in the name.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nominal_power_(photovoltaic)#Watt-peak

Yes, it is in Watt-peak and is the total installed watt-peak of the installation. So it is a fixed value (unless you add solar panels of course) that is send in the json data. The official solarlog documentation uses Wp as unit of measurement, 

If it is preferred to have this in Watt in HA, I’ll create a new PR tomorrow, no problem. I’ll change the capacity sensor than as well, from W/Wp to Percentage.
I think we should stick with scientific standards as far as possible.
Added a new PR with this change in #55110. Will update the docs tomorrow.
